metadata.title: Texas Instruments to buy Silicon Labs, Enphase stock surges 40%

content.text:
Market Catalysts Host Julie Hyman and Yahoo Finance Markets and Data Editor Jared Blikre track several of the day's top trending stock tickers, including Texas Instruments (TXN) purchasing Silicon Laboratories (SLAB) in a deal valued at $7.5 billion, Enphase Energy (ENPH) surging by over 40% on its fourth quarter earnings results, and Boston Scientific (BSX) shares dropping on its weak forecast.
To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Market Catalysts.
We are watching Texas Instruments and Phase Energy and Boston Scientific. First up, Texas Instruments. It is buying chip designer Silicon Labs in a $7.5 billion deal. That's the biggest acquisition for TI since 2011. It's expected to close, expected to take a little while to close, the first half of next year. Market's David editor Jared Blickry here with me now to chat through this and others. So, interesting that TI is making this move.
Yeah, it's been a while.
Yeah, it has.
And, uh, so this is, uh, going to be $231 cash for the stock of SLAB. That's a ticker there and we'll look at this charts in a second. Pitch from Texas Instruments seems to be this is going to deepen their embedded plus wireless connectivity footprint, bringing the smart home, industrial automation, medical power, all that together. SLAB focuses on connected device chips, which is in secure wireless plus mixed signal. They're used in smart home gear, metering, industrial equipment.
And why does this fit? Well, I think Texas Instruments is basically saying, we can make these chips ourselves at scale. Uh, Texas Instruments has fabrication. SLAB doesn't make their own chips as a lot of uh companies don't. And then TI can uh crosss sell those to some of their other uh customers, corporate, otherwise. So, as you said, this probably not going to close until next year, first half of 2027 and Texas Instruments says it needs about 450 million in annual manufacturing operational synergies within three years after the close. So there is some integration risk here. And if we go to the charts, we can see TI or TXN, only down about 1 and a half percent intraday. This is going to take a lot of cash on their part, as we outlined. But let me show you the five-year chart. I think they're up about 25, 30% this year, but they've just been in this trading range, especially over the last few years and it looks like they're trying to break out. Not going to probably do it today, but if things go progressively well, we'll we'll see, you know, maybe they can break out of here.
Then let's take a look at Silicon Laboratories and in this one day because the stock is up 49% today alone, it would it would have been break even, but here it is right back up at the highs that we saw in 2022. And I'll show you a max chart too, so you can see just been kind of trading in a range since, uh, the pandemic. And, uh, yeah, that about does it for my notes there.
Interesting. Um and well and it's also interesting because it's this is not an AI chip deal, notably.
Texas Instruments isn't AI, you know.
Right, it's the chips that go into like all of the other stuff. And they...
Yeah, for stuff we actually, you know, really really need on a day-to-day basis.
Yes, exactly. So shows kind of a a bet on that demand continuing. Um next let's talk about Enphase energy soaring after the company topped fourth quarter estimates, it issued a strong forecast for the first quarter. It saw increased demand for solar and battery installations. Remember the tax credit um is expiring for solar in the summer, for batteries at the end of the year. So just like it happened with cars when the tax credit was going to expire, there's a surge of orders ahead of that.
And there you go. They got the surge, uh but then you got to look past that at a certain point. but investors not doing that today. Stock up, uh pretty meaningfully. Let's just take a look at the stock first since that's what we're talking about. On the Wi-Fi Interactive up 41% today. I'll show you a five-year chart though and this isn't pretty because from the 2022 highs, it was down as much as, I think 90%, maybe only 80% but you can see over the last year, it is over the last few months, it has risen off of those lows and if you take out today's price action, I'm going to just kind of circle that there, doesn't look like much, but this is a step in the right direction. So, uh what does Enphase do? They build battery technology, so they they build the microconverters, uh that's the box that converts solar panel output into usable home electricity as well as home batteries and energy management gear.
And as to the earnings, so they beat expectations, um and the stock pop really about better than feared near term outlook. So even with those tax credits uh coming kind of uh evaporating in the near term. Q1 guide came in above street level and management framed quarter one as the demand low point. So it kind of gets better from here. I think that's the uh, that's the big uh, takeaway.
Yeah, and that's something analysts were looking for. And I misspoke by the way that the battery storage uh tax incentives actually last through the end of the decade, not through the end of the year. So it's the it's the rooftop solar leasing uh incentives that are going away this summer. Um and let's talk about Boston Scientific. Those shares are falling after the company issued a soft forecast for 2026. The medical device company's disappointing guidance overshadowing strong fourth quarter results.
I had to do a little um deep dive here because it was apparently the electrophysiology segment that was the most disappointing. Um this is something that they make uh pulsed field ablation. This is a apparently Got to love biotech. I know, apparently it's a treatment for atrial fi- fibrillation. Um and so that was the area that was most disappointing according to some of the analysis I saw.
Yeah, so I mean they got the beat on the quarter. The guidance, uh the stock reaction is probably about the 2026 growth guidance stepping down versus last year's pace. Organic growth outlook, 10 to 11%. This is slower than last year. EPS guide basically in line, slightly shy the midpoint depending on, you know, where you look, but not a huge uh deviation there. Traders focusing on the softer Q1 growth outlook and uh also the company is heading into a big integration with a prior purchase, that would be Penumbra. And uh so that's kind of part of the backdrop as well. So let's go to the chart here and I'll show you they're down 17% today. So that's that's not pretty. Here's the year to date and you can see they were already slightly negative here, but really in negative territory. I'll show you the five year. And this is a company that was and let's actually go to the 10 years so we can see the full pandemic. This is a company that started taking off um you know, 21, 20 in the wake of the bear market that we saw in 2022 and uh has just kind of fallen off after the third quarter of last year. Uh so
But still pretty good over the past, you know, over the past year.
Yeah. Basically doubled over the last five years including today's sell-off.
